interest: This file provides a clear, illuminating case study of how domestic agricultural and industrial interests mobilized congressional power—specifically through influential Michigan Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg—to task the U.S. Foreign Service with gathering competitive commercial intelligence during the Great Depression. It reveals the surprisingly rapid technological and agricultural development of Hokkaido's beet sugar industry in the mid-1930s, including corporate coordination between Hokkaido Seito and Meiji Seito to expand acreage and establish export channels to Western markets via Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha. Additionally, the practical descriptions of the imported pulp—noted as being packed in heavy bales 'hard as rock' that required sawing before use as cattle feed—offer an intimate, ground-level glimpse into international trade logistics and animal husbandry practices of the interwar era.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.61353) centers on an inquiry from the American domestic sugar beet and livestock feed industry regarding the nascent export of Japanese beet pulp to the United States. Initiated in early 1935 by the Farmers & Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association and the Larrowe Milling Company through Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg of Michigan, the inquiry prompted Secretary of State Cordell Hull to direct the American Consulate General in Tokyo to compile a detailed economic report. The resulting investigation, prepared by Vice Consul Charles A. Hutchinson, documents the cultivation of sugar beets on the northern island of Hokkaido, the operations of the Hokkaido Seito and Meiji Seito corporations, and initial export shipments of compressed beet pulp handled by Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha to the U.S. Atlantic and Pacific coasts. The file concludes with the transmission of the completed findings back to Senator Vandenberg, alongside an unrelated 1933 Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum regarding a Mitsubishi report on the Japanese rubber industry.

subfiles.about: Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg requests that Secretary of State Cordell Hull obtain a special consular report on the Japanese beet pulp industry on behalf of domestic agricultural interests.
subfiles.summary: Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg of Michigan writes to Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmitting an inquiry regarding the Japanese beet pulp industry. Vandenberg requests that the State Department obtain a comprehensive report on the subject through its foreign service officers. He asks that the completed findings be transmitted to him once received to assist domestic agricultural interests.
subfiles.title: Letter from Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg to Secretary of State Cordell Hull requesting report on beet pulp industry

subfiles.about: The Farmers & Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association asks Senator Vandenberg to solicit a diplomatic report on Japanese beet pulp production and exports on behalf of the Larrowe Milling Company.
subfiles.summary: The Farmers & Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association writes to Senator Arthur Vandenberg on behalf of Charles Staff of the Larrowe Milling Company in Detroit. The milling company expresses concern over new imports of dense, rock-hard Japanese beet pulp packed in 130-pound bales competing in the domestic livestock feed market. Finding Department of Commerce records inadequate, the association requests that Vandenberg prompt the State Department to obtain detailed figures on Japanese production, domestic consumption, and export volumes.
subfiles.title: Letter from Farmers & Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association to Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg regarding Japanese beet pulp imports

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull acknowledges Senator Vandenberg's request and confirms that the American Consul General at Tokyo has been instructed to prepare a report.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull acknowledges receipt of Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg's letter of February 2, 1935. Hull informs the Senator that instructions have been dispatched to the American Consul General in Tokyo to compile and submit a comprehensive report on the Japanese beet pulp industry. He promises to forward the report to Vandenberg immediately upon its arrival at the State Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg acknowledging request

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs the American Consul General at Tokyo to prepare a special report on the Japanese beet pulp industry with preferred attention.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits copies of Senator Arthur Vandenberg's letter and the enclosure from the Farmers and Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association to the U.S. Consulate General in Tokyo. The diplomatic instruction directs consular staff to treat the inquiry with preferred attention and use the enclosed correspondence for guidance. Consular officers are ordered to prepare and forward promptly a detailed special report answering the specific questions raised regarding Japanese beet pulp production and export.
subfiles.title: Instruction from Secretary of State to American Consul General at Tokyo

subfiles.about: Consul General Arthur Garrels transmits the completed special report on the Japanese beet sugar and pulp industry to the Secretary of State.
subfiles.from: Arthur Garrels, American Consul General, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: American Consul General Arthur Garrels in Tokyo transmits the special report on the beet sugar and pulp industry in Japan prepared in response to the Department's instruction of February 6, 1935. Garrels notes that Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha serves as the exclusive export agent for Japanese beet pulp manufacturers and was instrumental in supplying trade data. He informs the Department that further inquiries from the domestic sugar association may be addressed to Mitsubishi's branch office in New York City.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1935 from American Consul General Arthur Garrels to Secretary of State transmitting report

subfiles.about: A detailed consular economic report outlining sugar beet cultivation in Hokkaido, factory slicing capacities, domestic pulp consumption, export statistics to the United States, and expansion forecasts.
subfiles.from: Charles A. Hutchinson, American Vice Consul, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Compiled by Vice Consul Charles A. Hutchinson and approved by Consul General Arthur Garrels, this special consular report provides an extensive survey of Japan's sugar beet and pulp industries. Cultivation is concentrated on the northern island of Hokkaido, where two major firms—Hokkaido Seito Kabushiki Kaisha and Meiji Seito Kabushiki Kaisha—operate processing factories and plan additional facilities to double production by 1937. While beet pulp was historically consumed locally as dairy cow feed, surplus production led to export consignments beginning in late 1934, sending over 3,600 long tons to the U.S. Atlantic and Pacific coasts through Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha. An appended statistical table details annual seeded acreage, beet tonnage, refined sugar output, and pulp yields from the 1930–31 season through 1934–35.
subfiles.title: Report No. 137 on Production, Uses, Export, and Expansion of Beet Sugar and Pulp in Japan

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Cordell Hull forwards the Tokyo Consulate General's despatch and special report on Japanese beet pulp to Senator Vandenberg.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull writes to Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg enclosing copies of Tokyo Despatch No. 1935 and Vice Consul Hutchinson's special report on the beet sugar and pulp industry in Japan. Hull notes that the report was prepared in direct response to the Senator's inquiry on behalf of the Farmers and Manufacturers Beet Sugar Association. He expresses hope that the enclosed findings meet the needs of the domestic industry and offers further State Department assistance if required.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg transmitting consular report

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum commenting on a report on the Japanese rubber industry prepared by Mitsubishi's Economic Research Bureau.
subfiles.from: E. H. D., Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: An officer in the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (initialed E.H.D.) circulates a memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 716 of October 21, 1933, which transmitted a report on the Japanese rubber industry compiled by the Mitsubishi Economic Research Bureau. The writer advises colleagues F.R.D. and R.G.M. to skim the report to gain a broad sense of the scale of rubber manufacturing in Japan. However, the author explicitly recommends against expending effort on a close or detailed study of the material.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding Mitsubishi report on Japanese rubber industry
subfiles.to: F. R. D. and R. G. M., Division of Far Eastern Affairs
